title: Trust landscape mapper - notes (Olga)
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad to map Redwood-specific risks/control candidates to SOC2 criteria. This is intentionally loose — thinking out loud before we formalize control language for the evidence matrix. Aim: produce a 1-pager we can hand to compliance reviewer and link to ticket JIRA-SEC-987.

Context notes (product-specific reminders):
- Serving runtime: GPU pools, KV cache, batching. Key controls likely around access, change control to runtime, and configuration drift detection.
- Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private: different threat models (shared infrastructure vs customer-managed network). We need separate evidence buckets.
- Routing/fallbacks: automatic model fallbacks are a reliability control but also introduce complexity for change management and testing.
- Observability/Console: per-token cost/latency traces are stored — confirm retention and who has access.

High-level risk statements (brain dump):
- Unauthorized changes to model-serving kernels or kernel selection could lead to data leakage or prediction integrity issues.
- Misconfigured KV cache could expose cached keys between tenants (multi-tenant risk).
- Private deployments: customer-managed network may break telemetry; we need a way to attest that logs are retained for required period.
- Autoscaling/burst: capacity spikes could bypass quota enforcement causing billing anomalies and DoS surface.
- Rollouts (canary/A-B) without rollback gating could promote a bad model variant to production.

Candidate control ideas (quick names + evidence we can collect):
- Control: Runtime Change Approval (RCA)
  - Description: All runtime binary/config changes go through PR + signed release and documented canary window.
  - Evidence: GitHub PR + changelog, deployment tags, canary runbook snippet, rollback event if any.
  - Mapping: CC6 (change mgmt) and CC2 (logical access)

- Control: KV Cache Tenant Isolation Check
  - Description: Periodic automated test that asserts no tenant key collisions; config baseline enforced via infra-as-code.
  - Evidence: test run logs, IaC diff showing config, scheduled test job in infra pipeline.
  - Notes: For private deployments, provide template test to customer for self-attestation.

- Control: Model Rollout Gatekeeping
  - Description: Canary evaluation metrics (latency, failure rate, quality regression against eval set) must pass thresholds before wider rollout.
  - Evidence: Canary dashboard snapshot, eval-set run IDs, approval ticket (Jira).

- Control: Access Review for Console & Tracing
  - Description: Quarterly access review for console roles that can view per-tenant tracing/cost detail.
  - Evidence: Access review spreadsheet exported from IAM, reviewer signoff, list of role mappings.

Open questions / friction points to resolve:
- Evidence retention window for hosted API: product/infra currently keep detailed traces for 30 days — SOC2 wants 90/365 depending on control. Can we surface aggregated evidence for older periods? (ask storage infra — ticket to open).
- Private deployments: how to standardize attestations? Customers run different KMS/HSM. Propose an optional attestation kit (script + expected outputs) — needs engineering time.
- How to demonstrate separation between dedicated GPU pools (reserved capacity) for different customers? Need allocation mapping (pool -> account) and audit logs showing scheduling decisions.
- What counts as an "approved" eval set for rollout gating? Ownership and versioning? Link to research evals repo PR process.

Quick TODOs (short horizon):
- [ ] Add simple template for "evidence snapshot" that SRT/SEs can export on demand (single command). Samir to prototype. (JIRA-SEC-1012)
- [ ] Draft attestation kit outline for private deployments and route to solutions engineering. Lena/Arjun to draft. (linked to CONFLUENCE-TRUST-ATT)
- [ ] Validate retention windows with infra storage team and document exceptions (Olga).
- [ ] Map existing alerts to control IDs — pick 5 high-signal alerts that map to reliability/change mgmt controls.

Fragments / stray thoughts (delete later):
- Could we piggyback on billing events as proof of capacity isolation (billing+allocation correlation)? Might be weak as an isolation control but good for anomaly detection.
- For KV cache testing, consider a tiny harness that runs in each tenant's namespace during deploys — harmless keys then assert no cross-tenant reads.
- Consider labeling rollout artifacts with "SOC2:canary" tag so they are easily queryable for evidence collection.

Stakeholder nudges / who to ping:
- Infra-storage: Dana (confirm retention windows)
- Platform-eng: Haruki (audit logs for scheduler)
- Solutions Eng: Lena (attestation kit)
- Research/Applied ML: Samir (eval set ownership + gating thresholds)

Next steps (operational):
1) Convert candidate controls into table with control ID, description, owner, evidence artifacts, implementation status — target EOD Fri.
2) Create linked JIRA epic to track automation (evidence snapshots + attestation kit).
3) Run a 30-minute working session with platform-eng + infra-storage to validate assumptions (propose Tue 2026-03-04).

Notes to self: keep language non-legal in Drive doc — formal wording goes to compliance owner later. This doc should remain a living sketch.

End of page.

-- olga
